headline: Organic growth and margin expansion, GAAP EPS dips on taxes
summary_short: Aon's Q2 2026 revenue rose 2% y/y to $4.25B on 5% organic growth, but GAAP diluted EPS fell 3% to $2.58 on a higher tax rate; adjusted diluted EPS climbed 9% to $3.81 as the company returned $775M to shareholders via buybacks and dividends.
summary_long: Total revenue rose 2% y/y to $4.246B (5% organic), with Risk Capital up 5% and Human Capital down 4% on the NFP Wealth and Stroz Friedberg divestitures. Operating margin expanded 80bps to 21.5%; adjusted operating margin rose 70bps to 28.9% on organic growth, ABS scale efficiencies and restructuring savings. GAAP diluted EPS fell 3% to $2.58 as the tax rate rose to 22.0% from 15.5%; adjusted EPS rose 9% to $3.81 on higher adjusted income and fewer shares after $600M of buybacks. Cash was $1.06B; long-term debt fell 16% y/y to $12.9B. Free cash flow fell 34% y/y to $483M. FY2026 guidance reaffirmed: mid-single-digit-plus organic growth, 70-80bps margin expansion, strong adjusted EPS growth, double-digit FCF growth.

drivers.explanation: Management called it 'another quarter of strong performance,' citing the Aon United strategy and 3x3 Plan for accelerating organic growth, margin expansion, and capital return.
Growth reflects 5% organic growth from net new business and retention plus a 1% FX tailwind, partly offset by a 4% drag from the NFP Wealth and Stroz Friedberg divestitures.
Broad-based: Commercial Risk Solutions, Reinsurance, Health Solutions and Wealth Solutions each grew 5% organically on net new business and strong retention.
Margin expansion reflects organic revenue growth, ABS scale efficiencies and net restructuring savings, partly offset by continued investment in long-term growth.
Same underlying drivers as the GAAP margin move: organic growth and scale/restructuring savings outweighed growth-investment spend.
GAAP EPS fell as the effective tax rate rose to 22.0% from 15.5%, and the prior year included a $56M other-income gain tied to a legacy divestiture that did not recur.
Adjusted EPS grew on higher adjusted net income and a lower diluted share count (213.9M vs 217.3M) following $600M of quarterly buybacks.
Net income fell as the higher effective tax rate offset 7% operating income growth; the prior year also included the one-off other-income gain.
Not explained in the release for the quarter specifically; year-to-date operating cash flow growth was attributed to adjusted income growth offsetting NFP-related cash taxes and working capital.
The release cites lower total debt as a factor behind reduced quarterly interest expense, consistent with continued repayment activity.
